misses.query: I need to rebuild the old Requiem-Apocalypse patch against Apocalypse 10.2.3 — the old patch is disabled in MO2 but still on disk. Figure out what deltas it applied and re-apply the still-valid ones onto the new baseline.
misses.diagnosis: D's patch-rebuild clause ("wants a compatibility patch rebuilt against a new mod version") sits last in a long comma-chain after five catalogue/audit examples, so it read as a catalogue skill; the Requiem framing then made the agent hunt for absent mod-specific balance knowledge and fall through to N rather than recognise the delta-extract-and-reapply job D actually owns.

revalidation_2026-07-28_294.adjudicator_notes: 18 rows scored (no row id 12 in the set). Recall 8/9 = 0.89 (>=0.80); specificity 9/9 = 1.00 (>=0.50); PASS. No reasoning-vs-pick overrides needed — every pick token matched its stated reasoning, including the one miss (row 3's reasoning explicitly rejects the whole menu on Requiem-domain grounds, never naming D's capability, so N stands as a genuine miss and not a token slip). Specificity is clean and well-separated: the near-neighbour rows resolved to their intended owners with no D contamination — schema lookup to G (10), slot-52 filter to K (14), SPID ini to E (13) — and D did not pull the three record-read/tooling rows (17, 18, 19) that involve records but not a many-to-one deliverable, nor row 16's crash-log request. Only structural weakness: the batch-patch-rebuild trigger, which is the one D clause that competes against mod-domain skills rather than against generic record tools.
